qns_content.text: Who proposed the Five Kingdom Classification system?

text_solutions: R. H. Whittaker proposed the Five Kingdom Classification in 1969. The five kingdoms recognised in this system are Monera, Protista, Fungi, Plantae and Animalia.

qns_content.text: Compared with many other organisms, bacteria as a group show which notable feature?

text_solutions: Bacteria show the most extensive metabolic diversity. Some are photosynthetic or chemosynthetic autotrophs, while the vast majority are heterotrophs that depend on other organisms or dead organic matter for food.

qns_content.text: Which combination correctly describes eubacteria?

options.text: No cell wall and no genetic material
A rigid cell wall and, if motile, a flagellum
A protein-rich pellicle and two unequal flagella

text_solutions: Eubacteria, or true bacteria, are characterised by a rigid cell wall. Motile eubacteria possess a flagellum.

qns_content.text: Which pigment makes cyanobacteria photosynthetic autotrophs?

text_solutions: Cyanobacteria possess chlorophyll a, similar to green plants, and are therefore photosynthetic autotrophs. They may occur as unicellular, colonial or filamentous forms.

qns_content.text: Which statement correctly describes members of Kingdom Protista?

text_solutions: Members of Kingdom Protista are primarily aquatic and are single-celled eukaryotes. Their cells contain a well-defined nucleus and other membrane-bound organelles.

qns_content.text: Which fungal group may include coprophilous members that grow on dung?

text_solutions: Ascomycetes may be saprophytic, decomposers, parasitic or coprophilous. Coprophilous fungi grow on dung.

qns_content.text: Which fungus is extensively used in biochemical and genetic work?

text_solutions: Neurospora is an ascomycete that is used extensively in biochemical and genetic work. Other examples of Ascomycetes include Aspergillus and Claviceps.

qns_content.text: How is plasmogamy brought about in Basidiomycetes?

options.text: By fusion of flagellated gametes inside water
By fusion of two vegetative or somatic cells of different strains

text_solutions: Sex organs are absent in Basidiomycetes. Plasmogamy occurs through the fusion of two vegetative or somatic cells belonging to different strains or genotypes, producing a dikaryotic structure.

qns_content.text: Which plant is mentioned as a parasite in Kingdom Plantae?

text_solutions: Cuscuta is mentioned as a parasitic plant. Bladderwort and Venus flytrap are examples of insectivorous plants, which are partially heterotrophic.

qns_content.text: Which symptom may be produced by viral infection in plants?

text_solutions: Plant viral infections may produce symptoms such as mosaic formation, leaf rolling and curling, yellowing, vein clearing, dwarfing and stunted growth.

qns_content.text: Which pair consists of partially heterotrophic plants mentioned in the chapter?

text_solutions: Bladderwort and Venus flytrap are insectivorous plants and are therefore partially heterotrophic. Cuscuta is also partially heterotrophic, but it is specifically described as a parasite.

qns_content.text: On what basis did Aristotle divide animals into two groups?

options.text: Presence or absence of a cell wall

text_solutions: Aristotle used simple morphological characters for classification. He divided animals into those that had red blood and those that did not.

qns_content.text: Why was the traditional two-kingdom classification considered inadequate?

options.text: It did not distinguish prokaryotes from eukaryotes.

text_solutions: The two-kingdom system did not distinguish prokaryotes from eukaryotes, unicellular from multicellular organisms, or photosynthetic organisms from non-photosynthetic fungi. Many organisms therefore did not fit properly into either Plantae or Animalia.

qns_content.text: Which statement correctly describes the proposed three-domain system mentioned in the chapter?

options.text: It divides Monera into two domains and places the eukaryotic kingdoms in a third domain.
It combines all five kingdoms into one domain.
It places viruses in a separate cellular domain.

text_solutions: The three-domain system divides Kingdom Monera into two domains. The remaining eukaryotic kingdoms are placed in the third domain, producing a six-kingdom classification.

qns_content.text: Which statement best describes the distribution of bacteria?

options.text: They are restricted to the bodies of animals.
They cannot survive in deserts or snow.
They occur almost everywhere, including extreme habitats.

text_solutions: Bacteria are extremely abundant and occur almost everywhere. They are found in soil and also in extreme habitats such as hot springs, deserts, snow and deep oceans.

qns_content.text: Which bacterial disease is correctly matched with its cause?

text_solutions: Typhoid is listed as a bacterial disease. Other bacterial diseases mentioned include cholera, tetanus and citrus canker.

qns_content.text: Kingdom Protista forms a link with which other kingdoms?

text_solutions: Kingdom Protista forms a link with the kingdoms dealing with plants, animals and fungi. Its members are single-celled eukaryotes and are primarily aquatic.

qns_content.text: How do the pigments of euglenoids compare with those of higher plants?

options.text: They are found only in heterotrophic forms.
They are identical to those of higher plants.

text_solutions: The photosynthetic pigments of euglenoids are identical to those present in higher plants. This allows euglenoids to photosynthesise when sunlight is available.

qns_content.text: Under suitable conditions, what structure is formed by slime moulds?

options.text: A plasmodium that may spread over several feet

text_solutions: Under suitable conditions, slime moulds form an aggregation called a plasmodium. This structure may grow and spread over an area of several feet.

qns_content.text: Why is food commonly kept in a refrigerator?

options.text: To increase the rate of bacterial fission
To reduce spoilage caused by bacterial and fungal infections

text_solutions: Fungi generally prefer warm and humid conditions. Refrigeration helps prevent food from going bad by slowing the bacterial and fungal growth responsible for spoilage.

qns_content.text: Why were bacteria and blue-green algae placed together with other plants in earlier classification systems?

options.text: All of them had a membrane-bound nucleus.
All of them possessed a cell wall.

text_solutions: Earlier classifications placed bacteria, blue-green algae and several eukaryotic groups together under plants because all of them possessed cell walls. This approach ignored major differences in cell type, body organisation and mode of nutrition.

qns_content.text: Sexual reproduction in protists involves which of the following?

text_solutions: Protists reproduce both asexually and sexually. Their sexual reproduction involves cell fusion followed by the formation of a zygote.

qns_content.text: Which is a stated use of diatomaceous earth?

options.text: Polishing and filtration of oils and syrups

text_solutions: Diatomaceous earth is formed by the accumulated silica-rich cell-wall deposits of diatoms. Because it is gritty, it is used for polishing and for filtering oils and syrups.

qns_content.text: What determines whether a dinoflagellate appears yellow, green, brown, blue or red?

options.text: The number of nuclei in the cell
The main pigments present in its cells

text_solutions: Dinoflagellates may appear yellow, green, brown, blue or red depending on the principal pigments present in their cells. Most members are marine and photosynthetic.

qns_content.text: Which statement correctly describes the flagella of euglenoids?

options.text: They possess thousands of cilia instead of flagella.
They have two flagella, one short and one long.

text_solutions: Euglenoids possess two flagella of unequal length—one short and one long. They also have a flexible, protein-rich pellicle instead of a cell wall.

qns_content.text: Which features form the basis for dividing Kingdom Fungi into different classes?

options.text: Mycelial morphology, mode of spore formation and fruiting bodies

text_solutions: The major fungal classes are distinguished using the morphology of the mycelium, the mode of spore formation and the nature of their fruiting bodies.

qns_content.text: In Ascomycetes, asci are arranged in fruiting bodies called:

text_solutions: Ascospores are produced endogenously inside sac-like asci. These asci are organised into fruiting bodies called ascocarps.

qns_content.text: Which set contains only examples of Deuteromycetes?

text_solutions: Alternaria, Colletotrichum and Trichoderma are examples of Deuteromycetes. Members of this group reproduce by asexual spores called conidia.

qns_content.text: Who named the infectious tobacco extract “Contagium vivum fluidum”?

text_solutions: M. W. Beijerinck showed that extract from infected tobacco plants could infect healthy plants. He called the infectious fluid “Contagium vivum fluidum,” meaning infectious living fluid.

qns_content.text: How are the capsomeres of a viral capsid arranged?

options.text: As cellulose plates on the outer surface

text_solutions: The viral protein coat is called the capsid and is made of smaller subunits called capsomeres. These capsomeres are arranged in helical or polyhedral geometric forms around the nucleic acid.

qns_content.text: Why were Chlamydomonas and Chlorella placed in Kingdom Protista under the five-kingdom classification?

text_solutions: The five-kingdom system places single-celled eukaryotic organisms in Kingdom Protista. Thus, Chlamydomonas and Chlorella, although previously grouped with plants and possessing cell walls, are included in Protista.

qns_content.text: What is the most common ecological role of heterotrophic bacteria?

options.text: They are the chief producers in oceans.

text_solutions: Heterotrophic bacteria are the most abundant bacteria in nature, and the majority function as important decomposers. They obtain food from other organisms or from dead organic matter.

qns_content.text: Which set contains only groups included under Kingdom Protista in the chapter?

options.text: Chrysophytes, dinoflagellates, euglenoids, slime moulds and protozoans

text_solutions: Kingdom Protista includes chrysophytes, dinoflagellates, euglenoids, slime moulds and protozoans. These organisms are single-celled eukaryotes and are primarily aquatic.

qns_content.text: How do chrysophytes generally remain suspended in water?

options.text: They float passively in water currents as plankton.

text_solutions: Chrysophytes are microscopic organisms found in freshwater and marine environments. They float passively in water currents and form part of the plankton.

qns_content.text: Where may amoeboid protozoans occur?

options.text: Fresh water, sea water or moist soil

text_solutions: Amoeboid protozoans may live in fresh water, sea water or moist soil. They move and capture prey by extending pseudopodia, or false feet.

qns_content.text: Which unicellular fungus is used in making bread and beer?

text_solutions: Yeast is a unicellular fungus used in the preparation of bread and beer. Most other fungi are filamentous and possess bodies made of hyphae.

qns_content.text: Which association represents mycorrhiza?

options.text: Fungi associated with the roots of higher plants
Methanogens living in the gut of ruminants

text_solutions: Mycorrhiza is a symbiotic association between fungi and the roots of higher plants. Fungi may also live symbiotically with algae, forming lichens.

qns_content.text: Which statement correctly describes the growth pattern of animals?

options.text: They continue growing indefinitely without attaining a definite form.
Their growth occurs only through spore formation.
They follow a definite growth pattern and attain a definite adult shape and size.

text_solutions: Animals follow a definite growth pattern and develop into adults with a definite shape and size. Higher animals also possess elaborate sensory and neuromotor mechanisms.

qns_content.text: What observation led Dmitri Ivanowsky to recognise the causal agent of tobacco mosaic disease as being smaller than bacteria?

text_solutions: Dmitri Ivanowsky observed that the agent causing tobacco mosaic disease passed through bacteria-proof filters. This indicated that the infectious agent was smaller than bacteria.

qns_content.text: Which disease was caused by the viroid discovered by T. O. Diener?

text_solutions: T. O. Diener discovered the viroid in 1971 while studying potato spindle tuber disease. The infectious agent was smaller than viruses and consisted of low-molecular-weight RNA without a protein coat.

qns_content.text: An organism is unicellular, has a well-defined nucleus and may possess cilia or flagella. In which kingdom should it be placed?

text_solutions: A unicellular organism with a well-defined nucleus is eukaryotic and therefore does not belong to Monera. Kingdom Protista includes single-celled eukaryotes, some of which possess cilia or flagella.

qns_content.text: An archaebacterium survives in an extremely salty habitat. Which combination correctly identifies it and explains its survival?

options.text: Halophile; a cell-wall structure different from that of other bacteria

text_solutions: Archaebacteria living in extremely salty areas are called halophiles. Their cell-wall structure differs from that of other bacteria, and this difference helps them survive under extreme conditions.

qns_content.text: A bacterium oxidises ammonia and uses the released energy to produce ATP. How should it be classified?

text_solutions: Chemosynthetic autotrophic bacteria oxidise inorganic substances such as ammonia, nitrites and nitrates. They use the energy released during oxidation for ATP production and synthesise their own food.

qns_content.text: An aquatic microscopic organism has a wall made of two overlapping silica-containing shells. Which additional statement should also be correct?

options.text: It is a diatom and may contribute to diatomaceous earth.
It is a dinoflagellate with stiff cellulose plates.
It is a euglenoid with a protein-rich pellicle.
It is a slime mould that forms a plasmodium.

text_solutions: Diatom cell walls consist of two thin, overlapping shells embedded with silica. Their indestructible wall deposits accumulate over long periods and form diatomaceous earth.

qns_content.text: A marine protist has stiff cellulose plates and two differently positioned flagella. If it multiplies rapidly, what may occur?

options.text: A red tide that may kill fishes

text_solutions: The organism is a dinoflagellate. Red dinoflagellates such as Gonyaulax may multiply rapidly, making the sea appear red. Toxins released by such large populations may kill marine animals such as fishes.

qns_content.text: A protozoan has thousands of cilia and a gullet into which food-bearing water is directed. To which group does it belong?

text_solutions: Ciliated protozoans possess numerous cilia whose coordinated movement directs water laden with food into a cavity called the gullet. Paramoecium is the example given for this group.

qns_content.text: In a fungal sexual cycle, plasmogamy occurs but the nuclei do not fuse immediately. What condition is formed before karyogamy?

options.text: A dikaryotic condition with two nuclei per cell

text_solutions: In Ascomycetes and Basidiomycetes, plasmogamy may be followed by an intervening dikaryotic stage before karyogamy. Each cell then contains two haploid nuclei, represented as n + n, and the phase is called the dikaryophase.

qns_content.text: A fungus has branched septate mycelium, generally lacks asexual spores and produces four spores externally on a specialised structure. Which class does it belong to?

text_solutions: Basidiomycetes possess branched, septate mycelium and generally lack asexual spores. Karyogamy and meiosis occur in a basidium, usually producing four basidiospores externally.

qns_content.text: A virus infects an animal. Which genetic material could it possess according to the chapter?

options.text: Both RNA and DNA in the same virus
Single- or double-stranded RNA, or double-stranded DNA

text_solutions: Animal viruses may contain single-stranded RNA, double-stranded RNA or double-stranded DNA. A virus contains either RNA or DNA as its genetic material, but never both.

qns_content.text: In a lichen, one partner prepares food while the other provides shelter and absorbs water and mineral nutrients. Which pairing is correct?

options.text: Both partners are autotrophic and prepare food independently.
Phycobiont prepares food; mycobiont provides shelter and absorbs water and minerals.
Both partners are fungi with identical functions.

text_solutions: The phycobiont is the autotrophic algal partner and prepares food. The mycobiont is the heterotrophic fungal partner; it provides shelter and absorbs mineral nutrients and water for the association.

qns_content.text: A prokaryotic organism possesses chlorophyll a, forms a gelatinous sheath around its colony and may fix atmospheric nitrogen in specialised cells. Which group does it belong to?

text_solutions: Cyanobacteria are photosynthetic prokaryotes containing chlorophyll a. Their colonies are generally surrounded by a gelatinous sheath, and some forms, such as Nostoc and Anabaena, fix atmospheric nitrogen in heterocysts.

qns_content.text: An aquatic microscopic organism floats passively in water and has a wall formed by two overlapping, silica-containing shells. Which further conclusion is correct?

options.text: It is a dinoflagellate and possesses stiff cellulose plates.
It is a diatom and contributes to diatomaceous earth.
It is a euglenoid and has a protein-rich pellicle.
It is a slime mould and forms a plasmodium.

text_solutions: The organism is a diatom. Diatoms are microscopic plankton whose walls form two thin, overlapping shells embedded with silica. The accumulated deposits of these indestructible walls form diatomaceous earth.

qns_content.text: A freshwater protist has no cell wall, possesses a flexible protein-rich covering and has one short and one long flagellum. How will it behave when sunlight is unavailable?

options.text: It will prey on smaller organisms as a heterotroph.
It will form fruiting bodies bearing spores.
It will fix atmospheric nitrogen in heterocysts.

text_solutions: The described organism is a euglenoid. Euglenoids have a flexible pellicle and two unequal flagella. They photosynthesise in sunlight but behave as heterotrophs by preying on smaller organisms when sunlight is unavailable.

qns_content.text: A marine photosynthetic protist possesses stiff cellulose plates and two flagella, one longitudinal and one transverse. What may result if red-coloured members multiply rapidly?

options.text: A red tide that may kill fishes

text_solutions: These features identify a dinoflagellate. Red dinoflagellates such as Gonyaulax may multiply so rapidly that the sea appears red. Toxins released by such large populations may kill marine animals, including fishes.

qns_content.text: A fungus has aseptate, coenocytic mycelium. Its motile or non-motile asexual spores are produced inside a sporangium, and sexual reproduction produces a zygospore. To which class does it belong?

text_solutions: Phycomycetes possess aseptate and coenocytic mycelium. Their asexual spores are motile zoospores or non-motile aplanospores produced endogenously in sporangia, while fusion of gametes produces a zygospore.

qns_content.text: A fungus has branched, septate mycelium. It produces conidia externally on conidiophores and sexual spores internally in sac-like structures. Which combination correctly identifies its class and sexual structure?

text_solutions: The fungus belongs to Ascomycetes. Its asexual conidia are produced exogenously on conidiophores, while sexual ascospores are produced endogenously inside sac-like asci. The asci are arranged in ascocarps.

qns_content.text: A fungus has branched, septate mycelium, generally lacks asexual spores and forms four spores externally after karyogamy and meiosis in a specialised structure. Which statement is correct?

options.text: It is an Ascomycete, and the specialised structure is an ascus.
It is a Basidiomycete, and the specialised structure is a basidium.
It is a Phycomycete, and the specialised structure is a sporangium.
It is a Deuteromycete, and the specialised structure is a conidiophore.

text_solutions: The features identify a Basidiomycete. Karyogamy and meiosis occur in the basidium, generally producing four basidiospores externally. The basidia are arranged in fruiting bodies called basidiocarps.

qns_content.text: Only the asexual and vegetative phases of a fungus are known, and it reproduces by conidia. What should happen if its sexual stage is later discovered?

options.text: It should be moved from Deuteromycetes to the class to which its sexual form belongs.
It should be transferred to Kingdom Protista.
It should be classified as a viroid.

text_solutions: Deuteromycetes include fungi for which only the asexual or vegetative stages are known. When the sexual stage is discovered and its relationship is established, the fungus is moved to the appropriate fungal class, often Ascomycetes or Basidiomycetes.

qns_content.text: Three infectious agents are examined: X contains nucleic acid enclosed by a capsid, Y is free low-molecular-weight RNA without a protein coat, and Z consists of abnormally folded protein. Which identification is correct?

text_solutions: A virus contains RNA or DNA protected by a protein capsid. A viroid consists of free, low-molecular-weight RNA and lacks a protein coat. A prion is an infectious agent made of abnormally folded protein.

qns_content.text: Which sequence correctly arranges the major discoveries associated with tobacco mosaic virus from earliest to latest?

options.text: Stanley crystallised viruses → Ivanowsky recognised the filterable agent → Beijerinck demonstrated infectivity
Beijerinck demonstrated infectivity → Stanley crystallised viruses → Ivanowsky recognised the filterable agent
Ivanowsky recognised the filterable agent → Beijerinck demonstrated infectivity of the extract → Stanley crystallised viruses
Diener discovered viroids → Ivanowsky recognised the filterable agent → Stanley proposed five kingdoms

text_solutions: Ivanowsky recognised the filterable agent causing tobacco mosaic disease in 1892. Beijerinck showed in 1898 that infected plant extract could infect healthy plants. Stanley demonstrated in 1935 that viruses could be crystallised.

qns_content.text: An organism is prokaryotic, photosynthetic and may occur as a unicellular, colonial or filamentous form. Which additional feature would support its identification as a cyanobacterium?

options.text: A protein-rich pellicle instead of a cell wall
Chlorophyll a and a gelatinous sheath around colonies

text_solutions: Cyanobacteria are photosynthetic prokaryotes containing chlorophyll a. They may be unicellular, colonial or filamentous, and their colonies are generally surrounded by a gelatinous sheath. Some forms also fix atmospheric nitrogen in heterocysts.

qns_content.text: A microorganism lives in the gut of a cow and contributes to biogas formation from dung. Which classification and habitat association are correct?

text_solutions: Methanogens are archaebacteria found in marshy areas and in the gut of ruminants such as cows and buffaloes. They produce methane and are responsible for biogas formation from the dung of these animals.

qns_content.text: A microscopic aquatic eukaryote has two flagella, stiff cellulose plates and photosynthetic pigments. Which observation would most strongly identify it as a dinoflagellate rather than a euglenoid?

options.text: The two flagella are one short and one long.
The organism lacks a cell wall and possesses a pellicle.
It becomes heterotrophic when deprived of sunlight.
One flagellum is longitudinal and the other is transverse.

text_solutions: Most dinoflagellates possess two differently oriented flagella: one lies longitudinally and the other transversely in a furrow between the cellulose plates. Euglenoids instead have a flexible pellicle and two flagella described as one short and one long.

qns_content.text: A protist lives in water, moves using thousands of short structures and directs food-bearing water into a gullet. Which organism and locomotory structure are correctly matched?

text_solutions: Paramoecium is a ciliated protozoan. Coordinated movement of its numerous cilia directs water containing food into the gullet. Amoeboid protozoans use pseudopodia, while flagellated protozoans possess flagella.

qns_content.text: A fungus has aseptate, coenocytic mycelium and produces motile spores inside a sporangium. Which combination correctly identifies its class and spore?

text_solutions: Phycomycetes possess aseptate and coenocytic mycelium. Their motile asexual spores are zoospores, whereas their non-motile asexual spores are aplanospores. Both are produced endogenously inside a sporangium.

qns_content.text: Two fungi both possess branched, septate mycelium. Fungus X produces ascospores inside asci, whereas fungus Y produces basidiospores externally on basidia. Which classification is correct?

text_solutions: Ascomycetes produce sexual ascospores endogenously inside sac-like asci. Basidiomycetes produce basidiospores exogenously on basidia. Both groups generally possess branched, septate mycelium.

qns_content.text: A fungus is initially placed in Deuteromycetes because only conidia and its vegetative mycelium are known. Its sexual stage is later found to produce ascospores. What is the appropriate taxonomic action?

text_solutions: Deuteromycetes contain fungi whose sexual stages are not known. Once a sexual stage is discovered, the fungus is moved to the class to which that stage belongs. Production of ascospores identifies the sexual form as an Ascomycete.

qns_content.text: An infectious agent is smaller than viruses, consists of low-molecular-weight RNA and lacks a protein coat. Which additional statement is correct?

options.text: It is a prion associated with mad cow disease.
It is a bacteriophage containing double-stranded DNA.
It is a virus whose capsid contains capsomeres.
It is a viroid first associated with potato spindle tuber disease.

text_solutions: The described agent is a viroid. T. O. Diener discovered it while investigating potato spindle tuber disease. A viroid consists of free, low-molecular-weight RNA and lacks the protein coat present in viruses.

qns_content.text: An infectious agent contains no nucleic acid and consists of an abnormally folded protein. Which disease association is consistent with the chapter?

text_solutions: The agent is a prion, an infectious abnormally folded protein. Prions are associated with bovine spongiform encephalopathy, or mad cow disease, in cattle and its analogous variant, CJD, in humans.

qns_content.text: A composite organism disappears from a highly polluted locality. Examination shows that its autotrophic partner prepares food while its heterotrophic partner provides shelter and absorbs water and minerals. What is the organism?

text_solutions: The organism is a lichen, a mutually beneficial association between an algal phycobiont and a fungal mycobiont. The alga prepares food, while the fungus provides shelter and absorbs water and minerals. Lichens do not grow in polluted areas and therefore act as pollution indicators.

qns_content.text: A fungus has branched, septate mycelium, produces conidia externally and forms sexual spores inside sac-like structures. Which group and common name correctly identify it?

text_solutions: The fungus belongs to Ascomycetes, commonly called sac fungi. Their asexual conidia are produced externally on conidiophores, whereas sexual ascospores are formed inside sac-like asci.

qns_content.text: In a lichen, partner X prepares food while partner Y provides shelter and absorbs water and minerals. Which additional observation would support the identification of this association?

options.text: It grows abundantly in highly polluted areas.
Y is the fungal mycobiont, and the association is sensitive to pollution.

text_solutions: In lichens, the algal phycobiont prepares food, while the fungal mycobiont provides shelter and absorbs water and mineral nutrients. Lichens do not grow in polluted areas and therefore serve as pollution indicators.

qns_content.text: An organism is heterotrophic, has a cell wall and obtains nutrients by absorption. Most members are filamentous, but some are unicellular. In which kingdom should it be placed?

text_solutions: Kingdom Fungi includes absorptive heterotrophs with cell walls. Most fungi are filamentous and multicellular, but yeasts are unicellular exceptions.

qns_content.text: A very small prokaryotic cell survives without oxygen and causes disease in plants and animals. Which structural observation would identify it as Mycoplasma?

text_solutions: Mycoplasma completely lack a cell wall. They are the smallest living cells known, can survive without oxygen and include pathogenic forms that cause diseases in plants and animals.

qns_content.text: An organism belongs to Monera but survives in an extremely salty area because its cell wall differs from that of other bacteria. How should it be classified?

text_solutions: Archaebacteria living in extremely salty habitats are called halophiles. Their unusual cell-wall structure helps them survive in these extreme environmental conditions.

qns_content.text: A saprophytic protist moves over decaying leaves and twigs, engulfing organic material. Under favourable conditions, what structure can it form?

options.text: A plasmodium that may spread over several feet

text_solutions: The organism is a slime mould. Slime moulds are saprophytic protists that engulf organic material, and under suitable conditions they form a plasmodium that may spread over an area of several feet.

qns_content.text: An infectious agent associated with potato spindle tuber disease consists of free, low-molecular-weight RNA and has no protein coat. Which conclusion is correct?

options.text: It is a virus crystallised by W. M. Stanley.
It is a prion made of abnormal protein.
It is a viroid discovered by T. O. Diener.
It is a bacteriophage containing double-stranded DNA.

text_solutions: The agent is a viroid. T. O. Diener discovered it while studying potato spindle tuber disease. Viroids consist of free RNA of low molecular weight and lack the protein coat found in viruses.

qns_content.text: A parasitic protozoan possesses flagella and causes sleeping sickness. Which organism and protozoan group are correctly matched?

text_solutions: Trypanosoma is a parasitic flagellated protozoan that causes sleeping sickness. Plasmodium belongs to the sporozoans, while Paramoecium is a ciliated protozoan.

qns_content.text: Two aquatic protists each possess two flagella. Organism X has one longitudinal and one transverse flagellum, whereas organism Y has one short and one long flagellum. Which identification is correct?

text_solutions: Dinoflagellates possess one longitudinal and one transverse flagellum. Euglenoids also possess two flagella, but these are described as one short and one long.

qns_content.text: An aquatic microscopic organism is photosynthetic, floats passively with plankton and possesses indestructible silica-containing walls. Which ecological conclusion follows?

options.text: It is a major decomposer of forest litter.
It is a dinoflagellate that necessarily causes red tides.
It is a methanogen involved in biogas production.
It is a diatom and is among the chief producers in oceans.

text_solutions: The organism is a diatom, a photosynthetic chrysophyte that forms part of the plankton. Diatoms are described as the chief producers in oceans, and their accumulated silica-rich walls form diatomaceous earth.

qns_content.text: An aquatic microscopic eukaryote floats passively with plankton and possesses a wall made of two thin, overlapping silica-containing shells. Which conclusion is correct?

options.text: It is a dinoflagellate and must produce a red tide.
It is a euglenoid with a protein-rich pellicle.
It is a diatom and may contribute to the formation of diatomaceous earth.
It is a slime mould that forms a plasmodium.

text_solutions: The organism is a diatom. Diatoms have two overlapping silica-containing wall layers and form part of the plankton. Their accumulated, indestructible wall deposits form diatomaceous earth.

qns_content.text: A marine photosynthetic protist has stiff cellulose plates and two flagella placed in different orientations. Which additional observation would support its identification?

options.text: One flagellum is longitudinal and the other is transverse.
Its wall consists of two overlapping silica shells.
It has one short and one long flagellum and lacks a cell wall.
It moves and captures prey through pseudopodia.

text_solutions: The organism is a dinoflagellate. Most dinoflagellates possess one longitudinal flagellum and one transverse flagellum lying in a furrow between the cellulose plates.

qns_content.text: An organism has a cell wall, lacks chlorophyll and obtains dissolved nutrients by absorption from dead organic matter. In which kingdom should it be placed?

text_solutions: The organism belongs to Kingdom Fungi. Fungi are heterotrophic, possess walls containing chitin and other polysaccharides, and absorb soluble organic matter from dead substrates or living hosts.

qns_content.text: An organism is unicellular, aquatic and possesses a well-defined nucleus and membrane-bound organelles. Which kingdom is the best placement for it?

text_solutions: Kingdom Protista includes single-celled eukaryotes. Their cells possess a well-defined nucleus and membrane-bound organelles, and most protists are aquatic.

qns_content.text: A bacterium encounters unfavourable environmental conditions. Which response described in the chapter may help it persist?

text_solutions: Bacteria reproduce mainly by fission, but under unfavourable conditions some bacteria produce spores. Ascocarps, plasmodia and basidia belong to fungi or slime moulds rather than bacteria.

qns_content.text: An infectious particle remains inert outside a living cell but produces new particles after entering a suitable host. Which explanation best accounts for this behaviour?

options.text: It takes over the machinery of the host cell for replication.
It divides independently by fission outside the host.
It produces its own cellular organelles before infection.
It obtains energy by oxidising inorganic substances.

text_solutions: The particle is a virus. Viruses are inert outside their specific host cells but take over host-cell machinery after infection to produce additional virus particles.

qns_content.text: A very small prokaryotic cell survives without oxygen and causes disease in plants or animals. Which structural feature identifies it as Mycoplasma?

text_solutions: Mycoplasma completely lack a cell wall. They are the smallest living cells known, can survive without oxygen and include forms that cause diseases in plants and animals.

qns_content.text: A prokaryotic organism contains chlorophyll a, forms colonies surrounded by a gelatinous sheath and may possess specialised nitrogen-fixing cells. Which group is described?

text_solutions: Cyanobacteria are photosynthetic prokaryotes containing chlorophyll a. Their colonies commonly have a gelatinous sheath, and some forms possess nitrogen-fixing heterocysts.

qns_content.text: An organism belongs to Monera and survives in an extremely salty habitat because its cell wall differs from that of other bacteria. How should it be classified?

text_solutions: Halophiles are archaebacteria that live in extremely salty areas. The cell-wall structure of archaebacteria differs from that of other bacteria and enables them to survive in extreme habitats.

qns_content.text: A composite organism contains an autotrophic partner that prepares food and a heterotrophic partner that provides shelter and absorbs water and minerals. Which further observation is expected?

options.text: It is generally absent from polluted areas.
It consists of a fungus and a plant root.

text_solutions: The organism is a lichen. Its algal partner prepares food, while its fungal partner provides shelter and absorbs water and minerals. Lichens do not grow in polluted areas and therefore indicate air pollution.

qns_content.text: A composite organism contains an autotrophic partner that prepares food and a heterotrophic partner that provides shelter and absorbs water and minerals. Which additional observation would support its identification?

options.text: It is generally absent from polluted areas.
It consists of a fungus and a plant root.

text_solutions: The organism is a lichen. Its algal phycobiont prepares food, while its fungal mycobiont provides shelter and absorbs water and mineral nutrients. Lichens do not grow in polluted areas and therefore serve as pollution indicators.

qns_content.text: A virus infecting a plant is compared with a bacteriophage. Which combination of genetic material is most consistent with the chapter?

options.text: Plant virus—generally single-stranded RNA; bacteriophage—usually double-stranded DNA
Plant virus—both DNA and RNA; bacteriophage—single-stranded RNA only
Plant virus—no nucleic acid; bacteriophage—both DNA and RNA

text_solutions: Plant viruses generally possess single-stranded RNA, whereas bacteriophages are usually double-stranded DNA viruses. A virus contains either RNA or DNA as its genetic material, never both.

qns_content.text: A fungus grows on moist bread, has aseptate and coenocytic mycelium, and produces motile or non-motile spores inside sporangia. To which class does it belong?

text_solutions: Phycomycetes possess aseptate, coenocytic mycelium. Their motile zoospores or non-motile aplanospores are produced endogenously inside sporangia. Rhizopus is an example.

qns_content.text: An organism stores reserve food as glycogen and oil droplets, obtains nutrients by absorption and generally possesses a filamentous body. In which kingdom should it be placed?

text_solutions: These features indicate Kingdom Fungi. Fungi are absorptive heterotrophs, generally have filamentous bodies and store reserve food as glycogen and oil droplets.

qns_content.text: A prokaryotic colony contains chlorophyll a, is surrounded by a gelatinous sheath and sometimes forms specialised nitrogen-fixing cells. Which group is being described?

text_solutions: Cyanobacteria are photosynthetic prokaryotes containing chlorophyll a. Their colonies commonly possess a gelatinous sheath, and forms such as Nostoc and Anabaena may contain nitrogen-fixing heterocysts.

qns_content.text: An infectious agent associated with potato spindle tuber disease is smaller than viruses and lacks a protein coat. What is its chemical nature?

options.text: RNA and DNA enclosed together by a protein coat

text_solutions: The infectious agent is a viroid. Viroids consist of free RNA of low molecular weight and lack the protein coat found in viruses. T. O. Diener discovered them while studying potato spindle tuber disease.

qns_content.text: A fungus produces asexual spores externally on conidiophores and sexual spores internally within sac-like structures. Which pairing is correct?

text_solutions: Ascomycetes produce conidia exogenously on conidiophores. Their sexual ascospores are produced endogenously inside sac-like asci, which may be arranged in ascocarps.

qns_content.text: An organism is multicellular, lacks a cell wall, ingests food and digests it internally. Which additional feature is expected?

options.text: Reserve food stored as glycogen or fat

text_solutions: The organism belongs to Kingdom Animalia. Animals are multicellular heterotrophs without cell walls, obtain food by ingestion and internal digestion, and store reserve food as glycogen or fat.

qns_content.text: A microorganism oxidises nitrites and ammonia, uses the released energy for ATP production and contributes to nutrient cycling. How should it be classified?

text_solutions: Chemosynthetic autotrophic bacteria oxidise inorganic substances such as nitrites and ammonia. They use the released energy for ATP production and help recycle nutrients such as nitrogen, phosphorus, iron and sulphur.

qns_content.text: An aquatic unicellular eukaryote has no cell wall, possesses a flexible protein-rich covering and has one short and one long flagellum. How does it obtain food when sunlight is absent?

text_solutions: The organism is a euglenoid. Euglenoids have a protein-rich pellicle and two unequal flagella. They photosynthesise in sunlight but behave as heterotrophs by preying on smaller organisms when sunlight is unavailable.

qns_content.text: A prokaryotic organism contains chlorophyll a, may form colonies surrounded by a gelatinous sheath and sometimes possesses heterocysts. Which conclusion is correct?

options.text: It is a cyanobacterium belonging to Kingdom Monera.
It is a euglenoid belonging to Kingdom Protista.
It is a fungus with absorptive nutrition.
It is a diatom with a silica-containing wall.

text_solutions: Cyanobacteria are photosynthetic prokaryotes placed in Kingdom Monera. They contain chlorophyll a, their colonies commonly possess a gelatinous sheath, and some forms fix atmospheric nitrogen in specialised cells called heterocysts.

qns_content.text: A microorganism is found in the rumen of cattle and contributes to the production of biogas from dung. How should it be classified?

text_solutions: Methanogens are archaebacteria found in marshy habitats and in the gut of ruminants. They produce methane and are responsible for biogas formation from cattle dung.

qns_content.text: A single-celled aquatic organism has a well-defined nucleus and reproduces sexually through cell fusion followed by zygote formation. In which kingdom should it be placed?

text_solutions: Kingdom Protista includes single-celled eukaryotes with well-defined nuclei and membrane-bound organelles. Sexual reproduction in protists involves cell fusion followed by the formation of a zygote.

qns_content.text: An aquatic microscopic organism floats passively with plankton and possesses two overlapping silica-containing wall layers. Which ecological and economic conclusion follows?

options.text: It is a diatom; it is a chief ocean producer, and its wall deposits form diatomaceous earth.
It is a dinoflagellate; it always produces toxic red tides.
It is a slime mould; it forms fruiting bodies in favourable conditions.
It is a euglenoid; its wall deposits are used for filtration.

text_solutions: Diatoms are photosynthetic plankton and are described as chief producers in oceans. Their silica-containing walls accumulate to form diatomaceous earth, which is used in polishing and the filtration of oils and syrups.

qns_content.text: Bacteria normally reproduce by fission, but two additional observations are made: some form spores during adverse conditions, while others transfer DNA between cells. Which interpretation is correct?

options.text: Spore formation occurs only in photosynthetic bacteria.
Spore formation aids survival, while DNA transfer represents a primitive type of sexual reproduction.

text_solutions: Bacteria reproduce mainly by fission. Under unfavourable conditions, some produce spores, while a primitive type of sexual reproduction may occur through the transfer of DNA from one bacterial cell to another.

qns_content.text: A fungus occurs in aquatic habitats or on decaying wood in moist places, has aseptate coenocytic mycelium and produces asexual spores inside sporangia. Which class and spore types are correctly matched?

text_solutions: Phycomycetes commonly occur in aquatic habitats, on decaying wood in moist places or as plant parasites. Their mycelium is aseptate and coenocytic, and they produce motile zoospores or non-motile aplanospores inside sporangia.

qns_content.text: A very small prokaryotic cell lacks a cell wall, can survive without oxygen and may cause disease in plants or animals. Which organism is described?

text_solutions: Mycoplasma completely lack a cell wall and are the smallest living cells known. They can survive without oxygen, and many forms are pathogenic in plants and animals.

qns_content.text: A parasitic protozoan has an infectious spore-like stage in its life cycle. Which organism and disease are correctly associated with it?

text_solutions: Sporozoans possess an infectious spore-like stage in their life cycle. Plasmodium, which causes malaria, is the example given for this protozoan group.

qns_content.text: A plant life cycle alternates between a diploid phase that produces spores and a haploid phase that produces gametes. Which terms correctly identify these phases?

text_solutions: The diploid sporophytic phase and the haploid gametophytic phase alternate in plant life cycles. Their relative duration and dependence vary among different plant groups.

qns_content.text: An infectious particle contains nucleic acid protected by capsomeres arranged in a polyhedral form. Which additional statement must be correct?

options.text: It is a viroid composed only of low-molecular-weight RNA.
It is a virus, and its genetic material is either RNA or DNA.
It is a prion made entirely of abnormally folded protein.
It is a bacterium with a non-cellulosic cell wall.

text_solutions: A virus contains RNA or DNA enclosed within a protein capsid. The capsid is made of capsomeres arranged in helical or polyhedral geometric forms.

qns_content.text: A photosynthetic prokaryote contains chlorophyll a, may form colonies surrounded by a gelatinous sheath and sometimes develops heterocysts. Which organism could belong to this group?

text_solutions: The features identify cyanobacteria. Cyanobacteria are photosynthetic prokaryotes containing chlorophyll a. Forms such as Nostoc and Anabaena may fix atmospheric nitrogen in specialised cells called heterocysts.

qns_content.text: A fungus has branched, septate mycelium, produces conidia externally and forms sexual spores inside sac-like structures. Which classification is correct?

text_solutions: The fungus belongs to Ascomycetes, or sac fungi. Conidia are produced externally on conidiophores, whereas sexual ascospores are produced internally inside sac-like asci.

qns_content.text: A composite organism consists of an algal partner that prepares food and a fungal partner that provides shelter and absorbs water and minerals. Which additional observation is expected?

options.text: It is generally absent from polluted areas.

text_solutions: The organism is a lichen. The algal phycobiont prepares food, while the fungal mycobiont provides shelter and absorbs water and mineral nutrients. Lichens do not grow in polluted areas and therefore indicate air pollution.

qns_content.text: Which set contains only vegetative methods of reproduction described for fungi?

text_solutions: Fungi reproduce vegetatively by fragmentation, fission and budding. Conidia and zoospores are asexual spores, while ascospores and basidiospores are sexual spores.

qns_content.text: A very small prokaryotic cell survives without oxygen and causes disease in plants or animals. Which observation would identify it as Mycoplasma?

text_solutions: Mycoplasma completely lack a cell wall. They are the smallest living cells known, can survive without oxygen and include forms that cause diseases in plants and animals.

qns_content.text: A marine photosynthetic protist has stiff cellulose plates and one longitudinal and one transverse flagellum. What may happen if red-coloured members multiply rapidly?

options.text: They may produce a red tide and release toxins harmful to fishes.
They may produce methane in cattle dung.

text_solutions: The organism is a dinoflagellate. Red dinoflagellates such as Gonyaulax may multiply rapidly, causing the sea to appear red. Toxins released in such blooms may kill fishes and other marine animals.

qns_content.text: An infectious particle remains inert outside its host but takes over host-cell machinery after infection. Which statement about its genetic material is correct?

text_solutions: The particle is a virus. A virus contains either RNA or DNA as its genetic material, but never both. Outside a suitable host it remains inert, while inside the host it uses cellular machinery to produce new virus particles.

qns_content.text: An infectious agent associated with potato spindle tuber disease consists of free, low-molecular-weight RNA and lacks a protein coat. What is it?

text_solutions: The agent is a viroid. T. O. Diener discovered viroids while studying potato spindle tuber disease. Viroids consist of free RNA of low molecular weight and lack the protein coat present in viruses.

qns_content.text: A parasitic protozoan possesses an infectious spore-like stage in its life cycle. Which organism and disease are correctly matched?

text_solutions: Sporozoans possess an infectious spore-like stage in their life cycle. Plasmodium, which causes malaria, is the example given for this protozoan group.

qns_content.text: A fungus is known only by its vegetative mycelium and asexual conidia. Its sexual stage is later discovered and shown to produce ascospores. What should happen to its classification?

options.text: It should be placed in Kingdom Protista.

text_solutions: Deuteromycetes contain fungi whose sexual stages are unknown. When the sexual stage is discovered, the fungus is moved to the appropriate class. The production of ascospores identifies its sexual form as an Ascomycete.

qns_content.text: A saprophytic protist moves over decaying leaves and twigs, engulfing organic material. Under favourable conditions it forms a large spreading mass, but under adverse conditions it produces resistant spores. Which organism is described?

text_solutions: Slime moulds are saprophytic protists that engulf organic material from decaying vegetation. Under suitable conditions they form a plasmodium, while unfavourable conditions induce fruiting bodies bearing resistant spores.

qns_content.text: Two infectious agents are compared. Agent X consists of free, low-molecular-weight RNA without a protein coat, whereas agent Y consists only of abnormally folded protein. Which identification is correct?

text_solutions: A viroid consists of free RNA of low molecular weight and lacks a protein coat. A prion is an infectious agent composed of abnormally folded protein and contains no nucleic acid.

qns_content.text: A plant-pathogenic fungus causes rust disease, generally lacks asexual spores and produces sexual spores externally on a specialised structure. Which classification is correct?

text_solutions: Rust fungi such as Puccinia are Basidiomycetes. Karyogamy and meiosis occur in a basidium, and basidiospores are produced externally on it.

qns_content.text: Protozoan X moves and captures prey using pseudopodia, while protozoan Y possesses an infectious spore-like stage in its life cycle. Which pairing is correct?

text_solutions: Amoeboid protozoans use pseudopodia for movement and food capture. Sporozoans possess an infectious spore-like stage; Plasmodium is the example given for this group.

qns_content.text: A fungus used extensively in biochemical and genetic work has branched, septate mycelium and produces sexual spores inside asci. Which organism and class are correctly matched?

text_solutions: Neurospora is an Ascomycete used extensively in biochemical and genetic work. Ascomycetes possess branched, septate mycelium and form sexual ascospores inside asci.

qns_content.text: An aquatic protozoan possesses thousands of short locomotory structures whose coordinated movement directs food-bearing water into a gullet. Which organism is the best example?

text_solutions: Paramoecium is a ciliated protozoan. Coordinated movement of its numerous cilia directs water containing food into a cavity called the gullet.

qns_content.text: A prokaryotic colony contains chlorophyll a, is surrounded by a gelatinous sheath and forms a bloom in polluted water. Which further feature may occur in some members?

text_solutions: The organism is a cyanobacterium. Cyanobacterial colonies commonly possess a gelatinous sheath and may form blooms in polluted water. Some forms, such as Nostoc and Anabaena, fix atmospheric nitrogen in heterocysts.

qns_content.text: A composite organism is absent from a polluted locality. Its photosynthetic partner supplies food, while its fungal partner provides shelter and absorbs water and minerals. Which conclusion follows?

options.text: It is a mycorrhiza and the plant root prepares food.
It is a lichen and can indicate air pollution.
It is a slime mould and forms a plasmodium.
It is a cyanobacterial colony and forms heterocysts.

text_solutions: The association is a lichen. The algal phycobiont prepares food, while the fungal mycobiont provides shelter and absorbs water and minerals. Because lichens do not grow in polluted areas, they indicate air pollution.

qns_content.text: A unicellular fungus used in making bread and beer is placed among sac fungi. Which combination of features is consistent with this classification?

text_solutions: Yeast is a unicellular fungus used in preparing bread and beer and belongs to Ascomycetes. Budding is one of the vegetative methods of reproduction described for fungi.

qns_content.text: A fungus is placed in Deuteromycetes because only its vegetative and asexual stages are known. What should happen if its sexual stage is later found to produce basidiospores?

options.text: It should be placed in Kingdom Protista.

text_solutions: Deuteromycetes contain fungi whose sexual stages are not known. Once the sexual stage is discovered, the fungus is transferred to the appropriate class. Production of basidiospores identifies the sexual form as a Basidiomycete.

qns_content.text: An aquatic microscopic organism has two overlapping silica-containing wall layers. Its indestructible wall deposits accumulate over long periods. Which use of the resulting material is correctly identified?

options.text: Polishing and filtration of oils and syrups

text_solutions: The organism is a diatom. Its silica-containing wall deposits accumulate to form diatomaceous earth, which is gritty and is used for polishing and for filtering oils and syrups.

qns_content.text: A fungus has branched, septate mycelium, generally lacks asexual spores and produces sexual spores externally on a specialised structure. Which combination is correct?

text_solutions: The fungus belongs to Basidiomycetes. Karyogamy and meiosis occur in a basidium, and basidiospores are produced externally on it. Asexual spores are generally absent in this group.

qns_content.text: A fungus grows on decaying wood in a moist place, has aseptate coenocytic mycelium and produces spores inside sporangia. Which organism could be an example?

text_solutions: The features identify Phycomycetes. Members of this class may occur on decaying wood in moist places, possess aseptate coenocytic mycelium and produce zoospores or aplanospores inside sporangia. Mucor is an example.

qns_content.text: A branched, septate fungus produces conidia externally and belongs to the class commonly called sac fungi. Which useful organism could fit this description?

text_solutions: Penicillium is an Ascomycete, or sac fungus, and is a source of antibiotics. Ascomycetes possess branched, septate mycelium and commonly produce conidia externally on conidiophores.

qns_content.text: An organism absorbs soluble organic matter from dead material, has a wall containing chitin and stores reserve food as glycogen and oil droplets. In which kingdom should it be placed?

text_solutions: The organism belongs to Kingdom Fungi. Fungi are absorptive heterotrophs, their walls contain chitin and other polysaccharides, and their reserve food is stored as glycogen and oil droplets.

qns_content.text: A heterotrophic bacterium is useful in food production, while many related bacteria decompose dead organic matter. Which pair of roles is described?

options.text: Conversion of milk into curd and decomposition
Formation of red tides and production of basidiospores
Production of ascocarps and nitrogen fixation in heterocysts

text_solutions: Some heterotrophic bacteria help convert milk into curd. Most heterotrophic bacteria act as important decomposers and obtain nutrients from dead organic matter.

qns_content.text: A photosynthetic prokaryote contains chlorophyll a, may form blooms in polluted water and sometimes possesses specialised nitrogen-fixing cells. Which group is described?

text_solutions: Cyanobacteria are photosynthetic prokaryotes containing chlorophyll a. Their colonies may form blooms in polluted water, and some members fix atmospheric nitrogen in heterocysts.

qns_content.text: A fungus is initially classified among imperfect fungi because only its vegetative mycelium and conidia are known. Its sexual stage is later found to produce ascospores. What should happen?

options.text: It should be placed in Kingdom Protista.

text_solutions: Deuteromycetes contain fungi whose sexual stages are unknown. When the sexual stage is discovered, the fungus is transferred to the appropriate class. The production of ascospores identifies it as an Ascomycete.

qns_content.text: An organism is multicellular, lacks a cell wall, ingests food and digests it internally. Which reserve materials are expected?

text_solutions: The organism belongs to Kingdom Animalia. Animals are multicellular heterotrophs without cell walls, ingest and internally digest food, and store reserve food as glycogen or fat.

qns_content.text: A composite organism contains an autotrophic partner that prepares food and a fungal partner that provides shelter and absorbs water and minerals. Which observation is most consistent with its identity?

options.text: It is generally absent from polluted areas.
It consists of a fungus and a plant root.

text_solutions: The organism is a lichen. Its algal phycobiont prepares food, while its fungal mycobiont provides shelter and absorbs water and mineral nutrients. Lichens do not grow in polluted areas and therefore indicate air pollution.

qns_content.text: An organism absorbs soluble organic matter, possesses a wall containing chitin and stores food as glycogen and oil droplets. In which kingdom should it be placed?

text_solutions: The organism belongs to Kingdom Fungi. Fungi are absorptive heterotrophs, their walls contain chitin and other polysaccharides, and their reserve food is stored as glycogen and oil droplets.

qns_content.text: Protozoan X captures prey using pseudopodia, protozoan Y directs food-bearing water into a gullet using cilia, and protozoan Z has an infectious spore-like stage. Which identification is correct?

text_solutions: Amoeboid protozoans use pseudopodia for movement and food capture. Ciliated protozoans use coordinated cilia to direct food-bearing water into a gullet, while sporozoans possess an infectious spore-like stage in their life cycle.

qns_content.text: Bacteria normally reproduce by fission. Under different circumstances, some form spores while others transfer DNA between cells. Which interpretation is correct?

options.text: Spore formation aids survival, while DNA transfer represents a primitive type of sexual reproduction.
Spore formation is the usual method of bacterial multiplication.
DNA transfer produces a multicellular bacterial body.

text_solutions: Bacteria reproduce mainly by fission. Some produce spores under unfavourable conditions, while a primitive type of sexual reproduction may occur through the transfer of DNA from one bacterial cell to another.

qns_content.text: An aquatic microscopic eukaryote floats passively with plankton and has two overlapping silica-containing wall layers. Which conclusion follows?

options.text: It is a dinoflagellate that necessarily causes a red tide.
It is a euglenoid with a protein-rich pellicle.
It is a slime mould that forms a plasmodium.
It is a diatom whose wall deposits may form diatomaceous earth.

text_solutions: The organism is a diatom. Diatoms have two thin, overlapping wall layers embedded with silica. Their indestructible wall deposits accumulate over long periods and form diatomaceous earth.

qns_content.text: A freshwater protist lacks a cell wall, possesses a flexible protein-rich covering and has one short and one long flagellum. How does it behave when sunlight is unavailable?

options.text: It forms resistant spores inside fruiting bodies.
It preys on smaller organisms as a heterotroph.

text_solutions: The organism is a euglenoid. Euglenoids possess a flexible pellicle and two unequal flagella. They photosynthesise in sunlight but behave as heterotrophs by preying on smaller organisms when sunlight is unavailable.

qns_content.text: A group of heterotrophic bacteria includes useful forms involved in food preparation and other forms that recycle dead organic matter. Which pair of roles is described?

options.text: Conversion of milk into curd and decomposition
Formation of red tides and production of spores in asci

text_solutions: Some heterotrophic bacteria help convert milk into curd. Most heterotrophic bacteria act as important decomposers and obtain nutrients from dead organic matter.

qns_content.text: An infectious agent associated with potato spindle tuber disease is smaller than viruses and lacks a protein coat. Which description identifies it correctly?

options.text: A prion consisting of abnormally folded protein
A viroid consisting of free RNA of low molecular weight
A virus containing both RNA and DNA
A bacteriophage enclosed by a cellular wall

text_solutions: The agent is a viroid. T. O. Diener discovered viroids while studying potato spindle tuber disease. Viroids consist of free RNA of low molecular weight and lack the protein coat found in viruses.

qns_content.text: Which sequence correctly represents the major events of sexual reproduction in fungi?

text_solutions: Fungal sexual reproduction involves plasmogamy, or fusion of protoplasms; karyogamy, or fusion of nuclei; and meiosis in the zygote, which produces haploid spores.

qns_content.text: An infectious particle remains inert outside a living cell but produces new particles after entering a suitable host. Which statement best explains this behaviour?

options.text: It reproduces independently by fission outside the host.
It oxidises inorganic substances to produce ATP.
It forms a plasmodium before entering the host.
It takes over the machinery of the host cell for replication.

text_solutions: The particle is a virus. Viruses remain inert outside their specific host cells but take over the host-cell machinery after infection to produce additional virus particles.

qns_content.text: Which of the following correctly matches the components of a lichen?

text_solutions: In lichens, the phycobiont is the autotrophic algal component, while the mycobiont is the heterotrophic fungal component.

qns_content.text: Which of the following organisms completely lacks a cell wall?

text_solutions: A cell wall is completely absent in Mycoplasma, which includes the smallest living cells known.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about viroids is true?

options.text: They lack a protein coat and consist only of RNA

text_solutions: Viroids are infectious agents made of low-molecular-weight RNA. They lack the protein coat found in viruses and were discovered by T. O. Diener.

qns_content.text: Which of the following groups has cell walls composed of chitin and polysaccharides?

text_solutions: Fungal cell walls are composed of chitin and polysaccharides.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is a characteristic of archaebacteria?

options.text: Presence of peptidoglycan in their cell walls

text_solutions: Archaebacteria occur in harsh habitats such as extremely salty areas, hot springs and marshy areas. Their different cell wall structure supports survival under these conditions.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is an example of a parasitic protozoan?

text_solutions: Plasmodium is a parasitic sporozoan with an infectious spore-like stage in its life cycle and causes malaria.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is a characteristic of chrysophytes?

text_solutions: Chrysophytes include diatoms and golden algae (desmids). Most are photosynthetic, microscopic and occur as plankton in fresh water and marine environments.

qns_content.text: During unfavourable conditions, what does the plasmodium of slime moulds form?

text_solutions: During unfavourable conditions, the plasmodium forms fruiting bodies that bear resistant, air-dispersed spores at their tips.

qns_content.text: What is the mode of nutrition in slime moulds?

text_solutions: Slime moulds are saprophytic protists that move over decaying twigs and leaves and engulf organic material.

qns_content.text: Which fungal class is called "imperfect fungi" because only its asexual or vegetative phases are known?

text_solutions: Deuteromycetes are called imperfect fungi because only their asexual or vegetative phases are known. They reproduce by asexual spores called conidia.

qns_content.text: Which group of fungi is commonly known as “imperfect fungi” because only its asexual or vegetative phases are known?

text_solutions: Deuteromycetes are called imperfect fungi because only their asexual or vegetative phases are known. When their sexual forms are discovered, they are moved to the fungal classes to which they correctly belong.

qns_content.text: Which of the following organisms has a protein-rich pellicle instead of a cell wall?

text_solutions: Euglenoids such as Euglena lack a cell wall. Instead, they possess a protein-rich layer called the pellicle, which makes the body flexible.

qns_content.text: Which group of protozoans moves and captures prey by forming pseudopodia?

text_solutions: Amoeboid protozoans move and capture their prey by extending pseudopodia, or false feet. Amoeba is a common example of this group.

qns_content.text: What is the main mode of reproduction in bacteria?

text_solutions: Bacteria reproduce mainly by fission. Under unfavourable conditions, some bacteria may also produce spores, and a primitive type of DNA transfer may occur between bacterial cells.

qns_content.text: Which statement correctly describes the genetic material of viruses?

options.text: Every virus contains both RNA and DNA.
A virus contains either RNA or DNA, but never both.
Viruses contain only proteins and no genetic material.

text_solutions: Viruses contain genetic material in the form of either RNA or DNA. No virus contains both RNA and DNA. The nucleic acid is enclosed by a protein coat called the capsid.

qns_content.text: Which organism can multiply rapidly and cause red tides in the sea?

text_solutions: Red dinoflagellates such as Gonyaulax may multiply so rapidly that the sea appears red. Toxins released by these large populations may kill marine animals such as fishes.

qns_content.text: Which fungus is mentioned as a source of antibiotics?

text_solutions: Penicillium is mentioned as a source of antibiotics. In contrast, Puccinia causes wheat rust, while Rhizopus is commonly known as bread mould.

qns_content.text: Which group includes organisms whose cell walls are embedded with silica?

text_solutions: Diatom cell walls form two thin, overlapping shells and are embedded with silica, making them indestructible. Their accumulated cell-wall deposits form diatomaceous earth.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about cyanobacteria is incorrect?

options.text: They have chlorophyll a and are photosynthetic autotrophs.
Some can fix atmospheric nitrogen in heterocysts.
They may be unicellular, colonial or filamentous.

text_solutions: Cyanobacteria are prokaryotic members of Kingdom Monera and therefore do not possess a well-defined nucleus. Some forms, such as Nostoc and Anabaena, fix atmospheric nitrogen in specialised cells called heterocysts.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is a characteristic of Mycoplasma?

options.text: It is among the smallest living cells known.
It has a cell wall containing peptidoglycan.

text_solutions: Mycoplasma completely lacks a cell wall and includes the smallest living cells known. These organisms can also survive without oxygen, and many are pathogenic in animals and plants.

qns_content.text: Which of the following best explains why fungi are classified separately from plants?

options.text: Fungi are heterotrophic and have chitinous cell walls.

text_solutions: Fungi are heterotrophic organisms, whereas green plants are autotrophic. Their cell walls also differ: fungal walls contain chitin, while plant cell walls are mainly cellulosic. These differences support their placement in separate kingdoms.

qns_content.text: Which combination correctly describes the mycelium of Phycomycetes?

text_solutions: The mycelium of Phycomycetes is aseptate and coenocytic. This means that the hyphae lack cross walls and contain multinucleated cytoplasm within a continuous tube.

qns_content.text: Why are lichens considered good pollution indicators?

options.text: They do not grow in polluted areas.

text_solutions: Lichens do not grow in polluted areas. Therefore, their absence from a locality can indicate the presence of environmental pollution.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is a flagellated protozoan?

text_solutions: Trypanosoma is a flagellated protozoan. Members of this group may be free-living or parasitic and possess flagella; parasitic forms can cause diseases such as sleeping sickness.

qns_content.text: In ciliated protozoans, what directs water laden with food into the gullet?

text_solutions: Ciliated protozoans possess numerous cilia. The coordinated movement of rows of cilia steers water carrying food into a cavity called the gullet. Paramoecium is an example.

qns_content.text: Which group of archaebacteria is responsible for methane production from the dung of ruminants?

text_solutions: Methanogens occur in the gut of ruminants such as cows and buffaloes. They are responsible for producing methane, or biogas, from the dung of these animals.

qns_content.text: Which statement correctly describes spore formation in Ascomycetes?

text_solutions: In Ascomycetes, asexual spores called conidia are produced exogenously on special mycelium called conidiophores. Their sexual spores, the ascospores, are produced endogenously inside sac-like asci.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about prions is incorrect?

options.text: They contain DNA as their genetic material.
They are associated with bovine spongiform encephalopathy.

text_solutions: Prions are infectious agents consisting of abnormally folded protein, not DNA. They are associated with neurological diseases such as bovine spongiform encephalopathy, commonly called mad cow disease.

qns_content.text: In which kingdom do organisms generally store food reserves as glycogen or fat?

text_solutions: Members of Kingdom Animalia are multicellular, heterotrophic eukaryotes whose cells lack cell walls. They store food reserves as glycogen or fat and generally show holozoic nutrition.

qns_content.text: Where are basidiospores produced in Basidiomycetes?

text_solutions: In Basidiomycetes, karyogamy and meiosis occur in the basidium, usually producing four basidiospores. These spores are formed exogenously on the basidium, and the basidia are arranged in basidiocarps.

qns_content.text: What is the ecological role of chemosynthetic autotrophic bacteria described in the chapter?

options.text: They cause red tides in marine water.
They recycle nutrients such as nitrogen, phosphorus, iron and sulphur.

text_solutions: Chemosynthetic autotrophic bacteria oxidise inorganic substances such as nitrates, nitrites and ammonia and use the released energy for ATP production. Through these activities, they play an important role in recycling nutrients such as nitrogen, phosphorus, iron and sulphur.
